6. **Backups**: `worker/backup-schedule.ts`, backup job handling in worker/index.ts, retention, progress bars, where backups are stored (Proxmox storage name), `scripts/backup-vms.sh`, `scripts/verify-restore.sh`.
7. **Snapshots + restore**: `worker/restore.ts`, snapshot actions. What can go wrong.
8. **Monitoring/bandwidth**: `worker/monitor.ts`, `lib/capacity.ts`, bandwidth accounting models — how is bandwidth measured and enforced (or is it not)?

For each feature also name the Prisma models/fields touched. Report as dense structured notes with `file:line` for every claim. Flag anything unverified or simulated.

    kept billing. Reinstall already refused for this reason; restore had no guard at
    all. Added at both the action and the worker handler.

    detach deliberately keeps serverId so the disk stays owned by the vmid as an
    unusedN entry — which destroy_vm also frees. Fill a volume, Detach (the UI says
    "Data is preserved."), Reinstall: both guards saw zero, purge took the data.

    applied the term discount AND the seasonal promo. Upgrading cost far more than
    buying the same plan outright for the same end date: $1,044.45 vs $665.08 on a
    36-month term with a 30% promo — $379.37 overcharged. The mirror image was the
    downgrade CREDIT, which used the same undiscounted delta over an UNCLAMPED
    remaining duration, refunding more than was ever paid and multiplying it by every
    month a stacked renewNow had pushed expiresAt out — a money printer the moment
    the catalogue allows a downgrade. Both directions plus the client picker now call
    one shared client-safe function (lib/proration.ts), so displayed, charged and
    credited cannot drift apart again.

#!/bin/bash
# Nxeon — customer VM backups via vzdump
# Backs up all QEMU guests (running or stopped) with VMID in [100, 9000)
# to Proxmox storage "backup" using zstd compression, snapshot mode, keeping
# the last 3 backups per VM at the storage level. Templates (9000-9999) are
# excluded. Idempotent / re-runnable.
set -euo pipefail

STORAGE="${NXEON_VM_BACKUP_STORAGE:-backup}"
KEEP_LAST="${NXEON_VM_BACKUP_KEEP:-3}"

log() { echo "[$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z)] $*"; }

# Collect eligible VMIDs: numeric first column of `qm list`, VMID>=100, <9000.
mapfile -t VMIDS < <(qm list 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>1 && $1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $1>=100 && $1<9000 {print $1}' | sort -n)

if [ "${#VMIDS[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    log "no eligible VMs (none with 100 <= VMID < 9000); nothing to back up"
    exit 0
fi

log "eligible customer VMs: ${VMIDS[*]}"

# Optional dry-run: NXEON_VM_BACKUP_DRYRUN=1 only prints the selection/command.
if [ "${NXEON_VM_BACKUP_DRYRUN:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    log "DRY RUN — would run: vzdump ${VMIDS[*]} --storage ${STORAGE} --compress zstd --mode snapshot --prune-backups keep-last=${KEEP_LAST}"
    exit 0
fi

log "running vzdump -> storage '${STORAGE}' (zstd, snapshot, keep-last=${KEEP_LAST})"
vzdump "${VMIDS[@]}" \
    --storage "$STORAGE" \
    --compress zstd \
    --mode snapshot \
    --prune-backups "keep-last=${KEEP_LAST}"

log "done"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Restore-verification: proves the newest production dump is actually restorable.
#
# Restores the latest /tank/backup/db/nxeon-*.sql.gz into a scratch database,
# asserts that core tables restored with rows, then drops the scratch database.
# Production data is never touched. Exits non-zero on any failure so the
# systemd OnFailure hook alerts admins.
set -uo pipefail

BACKUP_DIR="/tank/backup/db"
SCRATCH="nxeon_restore_verify"
LOG="/tmp/nxeon-verify-restore.log"

log() { echo "[$(date -Is)] $*"; }
fail() { log "FAIL: $*"; sudo -u postgres psql -qc "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null 2>&1; exit 1; }

LATEST="$(ls -1t "${BACKUP_DIR}"/nxeon-*.sql.gz 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
[ -n "${LATEST}" ] || fail "no production dump found in ${BACKUP_DIR}"

AGE_H=$(( ( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "${LATEST}") ) / 3600 ))
log "verifying ${LATEST} (age ${AGE_H}h, $(stat -c%s "${LATEST}") bytes)"
[ "${AGE_H}" -lt 48 ] || log "WARNING: newest dump is ${AGE_H}h old (>48h)"

# gzip integrity first — a corrupt archive should fail loudly.
gzip -t "${LATEST}" || fail "gzip integrity check failed"

sudo -u postgres psql -qc "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null 2>&1
sudo -u postgres psql -qc "CREATE DATABASE ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null || fail "could not create scratch db"

if ! zcat "${LATEST}" | sudo -u postgres psql -q "${SCRATCH}" >"${LOG}" 2>&1; then
  log "psql restore returned non-zero; see ${LOG}"
fi
ERRS=$(grep -ci '^ERROR' "${LOG}" || true)
[ "${ERRS}" -eq 0 ] || { log "restore produced ${ERRS} errors:"; grep -i '^ERROR' "${LOG}" | head -5; fail "restore had errors"; }

# Core tables must exist and hold rows — an empty "successful" restore is a failure.
for t in User OsTemplate Plan; do
  n=$(sudo -u postgres psql -tA "${SCRATCH}" -c "select count(*) from \"${t}\";" 2>/dev/null || echo "x")
  [[ "${n}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail "table ${t} missing from restored dump"
  [ "${n}" -gt 0 ] || fail "table ${t} restored with 0 rows"
  log "OK ${t}=${n}"
done

sudo -u postgres psql -qc "DROP DATABASE ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null
log "restore verification PASSED (scratch db dropped, production untouched)"

### The "volid readback race"
`Volume.diskName` was ending up `null`, orphaning volumes (dead `diskName`, billing continues, guards blind).

**`07fdf16`** — layered fallbacks (verified diff on `worker/volumes.ts`): added `isRealVolid()` (`/opt/nxeon/worker/volumes.ts:81-83`, regex `/^[^,\s:]+:\S*vm-\d+-disk-\d+/`), added `diskVolids()` (`:86-95`), and replaced the single naive `volidOf(after[slot]) || volume.diskName || null` with a 3-tier derivation:
1. volid at the slot just written — `:182-185`
2. re-attach path: the known-good `volume.diskName` — `:186-188`
3. first-attach path: **the single disk that newly appeared** vs the `before` snapshot — `:189-194`

plus the never-regress write `diskName: volid ?? volume.diskName ?? null` — `:196-200`.

**`cab3581`** — the actual root cause. Verified diff: **"Proxmox applies a config POST ASYNCHRONOUSLY — an immediate GET can still return the pre-write view, leaving both the slot and the 'appeared' diff empty. That race is exactly how volumes ended up with a null diskName."** Fix = poll for the write to land before falling through: up to **10 retries, 1 s apart**, re-GETting the config until `isRealVolid(volidOf(after[slot]))` — `/opt/nxeon/worker/volumes.ts:176-180`.

### Reinstall wiping volumes / volume destruction — the guardrails

**`07fdf16`** added the first guards, both filtering on `status: "ATTACHED"`:
- worker `reinstall()` guard (before any status change or destructive call)
- `serverAction` action-level pre-check

**`29b4e50` (P0-4 + P0-5)** closed two holes. Verified from the commit body and diffs:

**P0-5 — reinstall guard asymmetry.** Both `07fdf16` layers counted `status: "ATTACHED"`, but detach keeps `serverId` set, so the disk stays owned by the vmid as an `unusedN` entry — and PVE's `destroy_vm` passes `include_unused => 1`, freeing those too. Attack path from the commit body: *"Fill a volume, Detach (the UI says 'Data is preserved.'), Reinstall: both guards saw zero, purge took the data."* `reinstallToOs` had always counted by `serverId` alone; the other two had not. Now:
- `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:438-452` — `findMany({ serverId })`, sandbox volumes filtered out (`diskName` starting `sandbox:`) `:442-444`, throws before any mutation `:445-452`. Rationale comment `:416-437`.
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions.ts:472-479` — `count({ serverId })`, throws `:475-477`. Rationale `:460-471`.
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:110-115` — `count({ serverId })`.

The advice also changed from **detach** to **delete/move**: "Detaching is therefore NOT sufficient protection, and telling the customer to detach was wrong advice" — `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:435-437`.

**P0-4 — `BACKUP_RESTORE` destroyed attached volumes.** `qmrestore --force` over a live vmid calls `destroy_vm` first ("avoid zombie disks when restoring over an existing VM"), which frees every volume the vmid owns including `unusedN`. Restoring an archive older than a volume silently wiped it while the `Volume` row kept billing. Reinstall already refused; **restore had no guard at all**. Added at both layers:
- Action: `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server-ops.ts:147-155` (`count({ serverId })`)
- Worker: `/opt/nxeon/worker/restore.ts:109-119` (`findMany({ serverId })`, sandbox-filtered, throws before the stop) — deliberately duplicated so a job queued before the action check existed still cannot destroy data (`:105-108`)

**Third path — full server delete is intentional teardown.** `remove()` deletes all `Volume` rows for the server and notifies each owner that billing has stopped — `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:379-395`. The disks were already purged with the VM.

**[FLAG] `Volume.inUse`, `Volume.mountPath`, `Volume.fsType` are dead fields.** Verified: grep for `inUse:` / `mountPath` / `fsType` across all `.ts`/`.tsx` outside `node_modules` returns **zero** reads or writes (the only `inUse` hits are an unrelated local variable in `worker/migrate-real.ts:1217-1236`). The schema comment at `/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma:712-718` says *"Safe-detach consults this; nothing may detach a depended-on volume without an explicit, informed override"* — `detachVolume` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-volumes.ts:147-164`) performs **no such check**. Detaching a volume that is formatted and mounted will still pull the filesystem out from under running services. The `useVolumeForDocker` consent flag exists only in the migration path (`lib/actions-migrate.ts:406`, `worker/migrate-real.ts:3347`), never on `Volume`.

### What can go wrong
| Risk | Status |
|---|---|
| `qmrestore --force` calls `destroy_vm`, freeing every volume the vmid owns incl. `unusedN` | **Guarded** at both layers (P0-4) — `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server-ops.ts:147-155`, `/opt/nxeon/worker/restore.ts:109-119` |
| Restore fails mid-way | Server left `STOPPED` (`:133`), then `BACKUP_RESTORE` ∈ `VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS` → `ERROR` on terminal failure. Disk state is whatever `qmrestore` left. **No rollback.** |
| Snapshot rollback fails | → `ERROR`; the restart at `:640-643` is best-effort |
| Restore over a **different** plan | **[FLAG] unguarded.** Nothing re-checks that the archive's recorded CPU/RAM/disk match the server's current `Plan`. The archive's own config decides where disks land (`/opt/nxeon/worker/restore.ts:136-137`), so restoring a pre-resize archive silently reverts `cores`/`memory`/disk size on the hypervisor while `Server.planId` still says the new plan — and a smaller restored disk cannot be re-grown by `resize()`, whose gate is `newTotalDiskGB > currentTotalDiskGB`. |
| Restore of an archive predating a `DISK_EXPAND` | **[FLAG] same class.** `Server.extraDiskGB` keeps billing while the real disk shrank back. No reconcile exists for this. |
| Restored root password | **[FLAG]** `Server.rootPasswordEnc` is not re-synced, so the stored credential can be wrong after a restore |
| Stale UI listing | `listBackups`/`listSnapshots` hit the env primary node only (see §6 flag) |
| Sandbox | Entire restore is a 3 s animation, no VM touched — `/opt/nxeon/worker/restore.ts:70-91` |

### Bandwidth accounting — **[FLAG] NOT MEASURED AND NOT ENFORCED**

Models exist:
- `Plan.bandwidthTB Float @default(1)` — `/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma:260`
- `Server.bwInBytes BigInt @default(0)`, `Server.bwOutBytes BigInt @default(0)`, `Server.bwWindowStart DateTime @default(now())`, `Server.abuseBwMark BigInt?`, `Server.abuseBwMarkAt DateTime?` — `:347-351`

**A repo-wide grep for `bwIn`/`bwOut`/`bwWindow` (excluding `node_modules` and `.next`) returns only these reads — zero writes:**

| Site | Operation |
|---|---|
| `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx:56` | reads `Number(bwInBytes) + Number(bwOutBytes)` |
| `/opt/nxeon/worker/abuse.ts:25` | selects `bwOutBytes` |

Consequences, all verified:
1. **There is no metering sweep.** `/opt/nxeon/worker/abuse.ts:8` claims *"Server.bwOutBytes, updated by the metering sweep"* — that sweep does not exist. Nothing in `worker/`, `lib/`, `app/` or `scripts/` ever writes `bwInBytes`/`bwOutBytes`/`bwWindowStart`. `bwWindowStart` is written **nowhere**, so no window ever resets.
2. **The customer bandwidth-usage panel always reads 0.** `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx:54-62` computes `usedBytes / (plan.bandwidthTB × 1e12)`; the numerator is permanently 0.

No `AbuseAlert{kind:"BANDWIDTH_SPIKE"}` can ever be created (`:50-59`), no admin alert (`:60-64`), and `abuse_autosuspend` (`:67-77`) is unreachable. Settings `abuse_outbound_mbps` (default 200) and `abuse_autosuspend` (default false) — `:19-20` — have no effect.
4. **No enforcement anywhere.** No overage billing, no throttling, no suspension on quota. `Plan.bandwidthTB` is display-only: `components/marketing/PricingGrid.tsx:30`, `app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx:124`, `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx:280-281`, `app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx:119-120`, `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:243`, `prisma/seed.ts:12-16` (1–8 TB across plans).
